body: When a slot falls inside a date override, this returns `true` early and never reaches the `busy.every(...)` check below. That means any calendar event or existing booking on a day with a date override is ignored, so those slots show as available and can be double-booked. Personal events always go through this path, because every user of a non-team event is `isFixed`. Instead of returning `true` here, fall through to the busy check (e.g. just skip the working-hours check).

`find` stops at the first override on the slot's date that doesn't contain the slot, and the slot is then rejected. If a user has several override ranges on the same day (e.g. 09:00-10:00 and 14:00-15:00), a slot inside the second range gets rejected by the first one. The check should be: "there is an override for this date and the slot is not inside any of them", i.e. `overridesForDay.length && !overridesForDay.some(contains)`.

This matches overrides to slots by the UTC calendar date of the override start (and `dayjs(...).format` here uses the server's local timezone while `slotStartTime` is UTC). A date override covers one day in the organizer's timezone, and for non-UTC organizers that day usually spans two UTC dates. Example: an organizer in UTC-8 with an override of 14:00-20:00 on day D covers 22:00 D to 04:00 D+1 UTC. Slots at 00:00-04:00 UTC on D+1 won't match, so they fall back to the regular working hours. Slots on the same UTC date that belong to a different organizer day get rejected. Compare dates in the organizer's timezone instead (`slotStartTime.tz(organizerTimeZone).format("YYYY-MM-DD")` against the override's organizer-local date).

This compares two different Dayjs instances with `===`, so it is always `false`. The "unavailable all day" override (start == end) is never detected here. It then goes through the range checks below, where a slot starting exactly at `start` (e.g. midnight) passes both conditions and is treated as available. Use `.isSame(...)`.

The containment check is incomplete. It only rejects slots that end at or before the override start, or that start strictly after the override end. So slots that partially overlap the override are accepted: one starting before the override start and ending inside it, one starting inside and ending after the end, or one starting exactly at the end. The condition should be `slotStartTime.isBefore(overrideStart) || slotEndTime.isAfter(overrideEnd)`.
Copy/paste bug: `end` is calculated from `slotStartTime`, not `slotEndTime`. Slots that start inside working hours but run past the end are accepted.

The slot is rejected as soon as *any* working-hours entry for that weekday doesn't contain it. But a user often has several entries for the same day: split availability like 09:00-12:00 plus 13:00-17:00, or the overflow entries that `getWorkingHours` creates when converting a non-UTC schedule to UTC. In those cases every slot is outside at least one entry, so all slots are dropped. This runs for every fixed host, which includes every personal event, so it's a serious regression. The logic should be "reject if no entry for that day contains the slot" (`!workingHours.some(contains)`). It also needs to handle slots that cross the UTC midnight boundary.

`hour()*60+minute()` wraps around after the offset is applied. If the shifted override crosses midnight in the invitee's timezone (e.g. organizer 20:00-23:00 UTC, invitee UTC+5, giving 01:00-04:00 the next day), you get a `startTime`/`endTime` that belongs to another day, or `endTime < startTime`. That produces no slots or wrong slots. In addition, `activeOverrides` above (line 206) is still chosen by the unshifted (organizer-local) date, so after conversion the override is applied to the wrong invitee day. Overrides that cover two invitee days need to be split, and the selection must use the shifted time.

`override.timeZone` is optional in `TimeRange`. If it's missing, `.tz(undefined)` uses the default/guessed timezone. `getSlots` also runs client-side (see the comment above), so that would be the browser's timezone, which gives a wrong offset. Also, `dayjs(override.start.toString())` goes through `Date.prototype.toString()` and back through a locale-dependent parse; just use `dayjs(override.start)`. Finally, `override.start` stores the organizer's wall-clock time labelled as UTC, not a real instant, so the offsets here are computed at the wrong instant. That can be off by one hour around DST transitions.
